messages:
incident-bot: URGENT ALERT — Dedicated pool `atlas-asia-01` (tenant=AtlasSure) reporting sustained GPU pressure. GPUs=8, util=98.7%, queue_length=124, avg_wait=18s, p95_latency=2.3s, error_rate=1.6%. Autoscaler status=blocked (burst_disabled). Paging @maria :rotating_light:

maria: ACK — paging @derek and @sophia. Severity: S2 for now. Need impact assessment and mitigation plan. Is this customer-facing errors or just queueing?

derek: I'm on it. Pulling metrics from prom and runtime API now. Quick snapshot: `atlas-asia-01` has 42k reqs in last 10m (baseline ~6k), spike started ~7m ago. Many requests are long-context generation jobs (seq_len ~2048). Queue shows many >30s wait. Not seeing OOMs.

sophia: Context: AtlasSure runs nightly model-health indexer that kicked off early after a config change on their side. It's mostly heavy batched requests hitting redwood-gen-13b. Autoscaler attempted to scale but `burst_enabled=false` on this pool (per tenant policy). Options: (A) enable burst to shared-hosted for short window (risk: noisy neighbor), (B) temporarily route AtlasSure to a quantized variant (gives perf improvement), (C) throttle/slow-start their indexing job from AtlasSure side.

maria: What do we need to do to enable burst? How fast can it take effect?

derek: We can flip `burst_enabled=true` for this pool via admin API; change takes effect in ~30s-60s. I'll prepare the command but need ops approval to allow cross-tenant burst. Also can push model substitution rule to route non-critical requests to `redwood-gen-13b-q4`.

raj: FYI @maria @derek @sophia — I'm on standby to notify AtlasSure if we do a mitigation that affects request behavior. They'll want a heads up before we change routing or enable cross-tenant burst.

emily: If this causes customer-visible latency/errors we should offer a credit proactively. Let's try mitigation first and communicate clearly.

maria: Given current numbers (queue 124, p95 2.3s, growing), authorize short burst for 15 minutes to relieve pressure and buy time to coordinate with AtlasSure. @ops-bot please run the enable-burst command for pool atlas-asia-01 -> allowed_burst_gpus=2 ttl=900s.

ops-bot: COMMAND RECEIVED: `enable_burst --pool atlas-asia-01 --gpus 2 --ttl 900`
ops-bot: ACTION: Updating pool config...

ops-bot: RESULT: OK — burst enabled for atlas-asia-01 (2 GPUs) until +900s. Audit id=aud_4555550000_1.

deploy-bot: Config change applied: pool atlas-asia-01 burst_enabled=true, burst_limit=2 (deploy id=cfg-4555550000-3). Rolling config to pool agents.

sophia: Monitoring after enabling burst: queue drops from 124 -> 38 within 45s, avg_wait 18s -> 6s, p95_latency 2.3s -> 1.1s. Error rate trending down. Looks effective.

derek: I've also pushed a routing rule to send small (<1k tokens) interactive traffic to `redwood-gen-13b-q4` for AtlasSure. That change is non-breaking and should further reduce load.

raj: I'm drafting a short message to AtlasSure: "We've detected an internal spike from your nightly job and enabled a temporary burst to stabilize latency; we're coordinating with you to confirm whether the job should be rate-limited. No data was shared outside your tenancy. We'll follow up within 1 hour with next steps." Want to run it by legal/comms?

emily: That sounds good. Add an offer of 2 hours of service credit for the instability, and a planned post-incident RCA.

maria: Noted. We'll keep monitoring. Next actions: (1) derek/sophia validate tail latency and error rate for next 15m, (2) raj notify AtlasSure with that message, (3) ops will keep burst window active for 15m then auto-revoke unless extended.

sophia: Quick note for follow-up — autoscaler blocked because tenant policy had `allow_cross_tenant_burst=false`. We should prepare a runtime fix that either auto-approves short emergency bursts for enterprise customers with SLA opt-in, or surfaces a 1-click approve workflow to oncall. I'll open a ticket.

derek: Metrics 10m after change: queue 12, avg_wait 2.1s, p95 0.9s, error_rate 0.2%. Burst consumed 1.8/2 GPUs. Stability achieved.

ops-bot: NOTICE: Burst TTL expires in 5 minutes.

maria: @lee — handing off monitoring to you (night SRE). Current state: stable after burst, routing fallback pushed, customer notified (message pending send by raj). If queue or error_rate climbs >50% of current spike, escalate to S1 and re-open this thread. Leaving incident notes in pager duty.

lee: Got it — I'll watch metrics and escalate if it reappears. Can we add a follow-up tomorrow to discuss permanent config change for AtlasSure?

maria: Yes — schedule a 1h follow-up with runtime and account teams. Also tag this for a postmortem if customer reports anything.

raj: Sent message to AtlasSure (copied): "We've enabled a temporary burst to stabilize your traffic; we see a large indexing job starting earlier than expected. Please confirm if you want us to throttle or if you'll postpone the job. We'll provide an incident summary within 24h."

emily: Customer reply (via email cross-post) — "Thanks, we're pausing the indexing job and will follow up with our infra team. Appreciate the quick mitigation." :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Burst TTL expired; revoking burst for atlas-asia-01. ACTION: revert burst_enabled to tenant default (allowed_burst_gpus=0). Audit id=aud_4555550000_2.

sophia: Post-burst metrics stable: queue 3, p95 0.7s. I'll file follow-up: (a) change autoscaler behavior to surface emergency approval, (b) add tenant policy exception path, (c) recommend customer backoff controls and a model-quantization fall-back rule.

maria: Closing active mitigation. Leaving thread open for any further updates. Final note: offer 2 hours credit and schedule RCA sync tomorrow 10:00 PT.

lee: Acknowledged, taking on post-incident watch.

maria: Thanks everyone. :tada:
